result.rule: Use data input and output associations between data and activities. Data associations do not define execution order.
Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use bpmn:subProcess for a nested workflow belonging to its parent process; keep all internal nodes and flows inside it.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.

args.text: When a description states that several distinct data inputs are collected to calculate one combined measure, model the collection as parallel branches that converge before the calculation.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers the parallel data collection and synchronization pattern.

result.rule: When the description says that one activity can be carried out while another activity or sequence of activities is underway, and that both tracks must be complete before a later activity can proceed: Model the tracks as concurrent branches, using a parallel gateway to split them and a parallel gateway to synchronize them before the dependent activity.

When the description says that several work items must each pass an evaluation before a later step can proceed, and that unsuccessful items require revision and another evaluation: Model an outcome decision for each work item, route unsuccessful items through the required revision and back to evaluation, and synchronize the successful paths before the dependent step.

When the description says that information is collected from an external device or system for use in a later calculation: Model the information retrieval as a distinct activity before the calculation, and use an appropriate BPMN task type for the described retrieval.

When the description distinguishes preparatory work from a subsequent review and describes findings identified during that review: Model the review as a separate activity before modeling the activity that records or addresses its findings.

args.text: When the description says that an ongoing monitoring process should continue after a device restarts, but terminate if the device becomes disconnected, model the restart and disconnection as distinct event-driven outcomes: resume the monitoring flow on restart and end the process on disconnection.

trace.reason: Check documented guidance on event-driven restart and termination outcomes before proposing a guideline.

result.rule: Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
Build a connected path from each modeled start to an end or intentionally continuing state. Avoid accidental disconnected flow nodes.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.
Use an interrupting event-subprocess start when the parent scope stops; use non-interrupting only when the parent continues.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.

args.text: When a description says that an ongoing process resumes when a device restarts but terminates when the device disconnects, model restart and disconnection as distinct event outcomes: catch the restart event and return to the ongoing work, and route disconnection to a process end.

result.rule: When the description says that work resumes after an external restart: Model the restart as an intermediate catch event and connect it by sequence flow to the activity that resumes the ongoing work.

When the description says that an activity continues while a milestone or other condition is pending, and that a later phase follows once the condition is met: Model a decision point after the activity: route the unmet outcome back to repeat the activity and the met outcome to the later phase.

When the description says an activity occurs repeatedly or continues over an ongoing process and separately states that another activity starts only when a condition occurs: do not model the ongoing activity as an unconditional predecessor of the condition-triggered activity; preserve their distinct timing and stated dependencies in the BPMN flow

When the description states that a notification or milestone can occur after process work has begun: Model the later trigger within the ongoing process as an intermediate catch event, not as an independent process start event.

result.rule: Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.
Use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger and an intermediate throw event when flow emits or raises a result.
Use bpmn:task for atomic work when the execution mode is unspecified. A task contains no internal flow.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use bpmn:callActivity only to invoke a separately defined reusable process or global task; make calledElement resolvable in the intended model context.

result.rule: When the description states a decision cutoff but does not specify its numeric amount: Preserve that level of specificity in the BPMN gateway label or condition; do not invent a precise threshold.

When the description states a specific activity, decision, or outcome: Label the corresponding BPMN element with wording that preserves the described action and its object or result; do not substitute a related but different action or outcome.
